public_rationale: Marcus forecast that OpenAI would find it hard to IPO at an even higher valuation. He set no deadline. OpenAI filed a confidential S-1 on June 8, 2026, and said it had not decided on timing. By August 2026 it had done a $7 billion employee tender at a flat $852 billion valuation and still had no public timeline. By the evaluation date OpenAI had not priced, withdrawn or repriced an IPO. Reports of a delay to 2027 are secondary and give mixed reasons, so they do not show the 'hardness' he predicted. With no deadline and no decisive event, the forecast stays open.
limitations: 'Hard' has no threshold. A strategic delay is not clearly the same as difficulty.
The baseline valuation he had in mind is unclear.

from_speaker: OpenAI wants to IPO at even higher valuation
given this news (banks balking at SoftBank's OpenAI-backed margin loan)
our_interpretation: Read as a forecast that OpenAI will have difficulty completing an IPO at a valuation above its last private mark ($852 billion post-money, March 2026).

No deadline was stated. 'Hard' has no threshold. Clear signs of difficulty would be: OpenAI withdrawing or indefinitely shelving its IPO for lack of demand, or pricing it at or below the last private mark. A clear contradiction would be an IPO priced comfortably above $852 billion with strong demand.
The 'given this news' part is the speaker's reason, not a separate condition. It is not scored as an antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: OpenAI withdraws or indefinitely shelves its IPO because demand or valuation is weak, or prices it at or below its last private valuation, or publicly cuts its valuation goal for the listing.
criteria.contradiction_condition: OpenAI completes an IPO priced above its last private valuation ($852 billion) without visible trouble over demand or valuation.
